title: Never Too Much
desc_lfm_album: Luther Vandross' "Never Too Much" is his first solo project. It was released in 1979 and the title track skyrocketed up the R&B charts. Although Vandross had sang back up for some of the music industries giants, his voice became popular after singing TV commercial jingles. He sang lead in a band called Change and even appeared on Sesame Street. His debut project shot him to superstardom in what seemed like over night... but this velvety voice had been around for a while. His following projects, such as Any Love, Busy Body, Forever For Always For Love, Give Me A .
desc_lfm_artist: Luther Vandross Jr. (April 20, 1951 – July 1, 2005) was an American singer, songwriter and record producer. Throughout his career, Vandross was an in-demand background vocalist for several different artists including Todd Rundgren, Judy Collins, Chaka Khan, Bette Midler, Diana Ross, David Bowie, Ben E. King, and Donna Summer. He later became a lead singer of the group Change, which released its gold-certified debut album, The Glow of Love, in 1980 on Warner/RFC Records.

title: Straight From the Heart
desc_lfm_artist: Keyboardist/singer/songwriter/arranger/musical director Patrice Rushen has had an outstanding career with several Top Ten R&B hits, including "Haven't You Heard," "Forget Me Nots," "Feels So Real," and "Watch Out."  Arguably she has received much of her popularity through other acts copying or sampling her material.  "Forget Me Nots" was the basis of Will Smith's "Men in Black" from the blockbuster movie of the same name on Big Willie Style and George Michael extensively used the same track for his hit 'Fastlove'.
